"""Short negative earnings-surprise firms when the report arrives during a synchronized sector downside-tail regime and the issuer has weak financing capacity. Investors process an earnings disappointment more aggressively when peer drawdowns make funding and refinancing risk salient, while mandate-constrained holders and volatility-sensitive capital are less able to absorb the stock; this creates delayed bad-news transmission rather than a one-day repricing. The signal fails if negative-surprise firms with fragile balance sheets do not have materially worse forward returns specifically during sector-tail synchronization than during ordinary sector conditions."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_tail_breadth_loo(
    close: pd.DataFrame, sector_labels: pd.Series, window: int = 60
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal leave-one-out sector breadth of idiosyncratic downside-tail days."""
    ret = close.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    lower_tail = ret.rolling(window, min_periods=30).quantile(0.15)
    available = ret.notna() & lower_tail.notna()
    tail_event = ((ret <= lower_tail) & (ret < 0.0) & available).astype(float)
    availability = available.astype(float)

    result = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    for group in pd.unique(sector_labels):
        columns = sector_labels.index[sector_labels == group]
        if len(columns) <= 1:
            continue

        group_tails = tail_event.loc[:, columns]
        group_available = availability.loc[:, columns]
        total_tails = group_tails.sum(axis=1)
        total_available = group_available.sum(axis=1)

        numerator = group_tails.rsub(total_tails, axis=0)
        denominator = group_available.rsub(total_available, axis=0)
        result.loc[:, columns] = numerator.div(denominator.where(denominator > 0.0))

    return result.fillna(0.0)


def _sector_rank(signal: pd.DataFrame, sector_labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Rank independently within static sectors, with neutral singleton sectors."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(0.5, index=signal.index, columns=signal.columns)
    for group in pd.unique(sector_labels):
        columns = sector_labels.index[sector_labels == group]
        if len(columns) > 1:
            result.loc[:, columns] = signal.loc[:, columns].rank(axis=1, pct=True)
    return result.fillna(0.5)


def _new_report_event(eps_surprise: pd.DataFrame, revenue_surprise: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Detect public surprise updates without looking ahead through quarterly steps."""
    eps_prior = eps_surprise.shift(1)
    revenue_prior = revenue_surprise.shift(1)

    eps_update = eps_surprise.notna() & (
        eps_prior.isna() | eps_surprise.ne(eps_prior)
    )
    revenue_update = revenue_surprise.notna() & (
        revenue_prior.isna() | revenue_surprise.ne(revenue_prior)
    )
    return eps_update | revenue_update


@register_factor
class FragileEarningsTailRegimeTransmission(BaseFactor):
    """Conditional bad-news transmission under sector tail stress and financing fragility."""

    factor_id = "fragile_earnings_tail_regime_transmission"
    name = "Fragile Earnings Tail Transmission"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Within-sector rank of fresh negative EPS/revenue surprises, activated only "
        "when leave-one-out sector downside-tail breadth is elevated and scaled by "
        "balance-sheet financing fragility; lower ranks identify conditional shorts."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "sector",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "netDebtToEbitda",
        "currentRatio",
        "interestCoverage",
        "debtGrowth",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        sector_frame = data["sector"]
        sector_labels = sector_frame.iloc[0].astype(object).fillna("Unknown")

        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"].reindex_like(close)
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"].reindex_like(close)

        report_event = _new_report_event(eps_surprise, revenue_surprise)
        event_decay = report_event.astype(float).rolling(6, min_periods=1).max()

        eps_available = eps_surprise.notna().astype(float)
        revenue_available = revenue_surprise.notna().astype(float)
        surprise_count = eps_available + revenue_available
        signed_news = (
            np.sign(eps_surprise.fillna(0.0))
            + np.sign(revenue_surprise.fillna(0.0))
        ).div(surprise_count.where(surprise_count > 0.0))
        negative_news = signed_news.clip(upper=0.0).fillna(0.0)

        net_debt_rank = data["netDebtToEbitda"].reindex_like(close).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        current_ratio_rank = data["currentRatio"].reindex_like(close).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        coverage_rank = data["interestCoverage"].reindex_like(close).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        debt_growth_rank = data["debtGrowth"].reindex_like(close).rank(axis=1, pct=True)

        fragility = (
            net_debt_rank.fillna(0.5)
            + (1.0 - current_ratio_rank.fillna(0.5))
            + (1.0 - coverage_rank.fillna(0.5))
            + debt_growth_rank.fillna(0.5)
        ) / 4.0

        breadth = _sector_tail_breadth_loo(close, sector_labels, 60)
        tail_regime = ((breadth - 0.10) / 0.40).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        raw_signal = negative_news * event_decay * tail_regime * (0.5 + fragility)
        return _sector_rank(raw_signal.fillna(0.0), sector_labels)

"""Bad-news shocks can create self-exciting selling when a negative return innovation is unusually large relative to the stock's own recent volatility, especially when the close remains near the session low. Firms with weak cash coverage, high leverage, and poor operating-cash-flow quality are less able to reassure marginal investors, so the downside excitation should persist for several days rather than mean-revert immediately. The other side of the trade is liquidity providers and value-oriented buyers who underestimate the interaction between a fragile balance sheet and clustered downside flow; the thesis is falsified if negative-tail persistence is no stronger among financially fragile firms than among financially buffered firms."""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _tail_excitation_imbalance(close: pd.DataFrame, high: pd.DataFrame, low: pd.DataFrame, volume: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal exponentially decayed signed tail-flow imbalance.

    Negative standardized innovations are weighted most heavily when the close
    is near the bar low and volume is surprising.  Positive innovations receive
    the symmetric close-near-high weight.  Separate EWM kernels approximate the
    persistent excitation of same-signed order flow.
    """
    safe_close = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    ret = safe_close.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    ret_vol = ret.rolling(23, min_periods=10).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    innovation = (ret / ret_vol).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
    bar_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    close_location = ((close - low) / bar_range).clip(0.0, 1.0)
    close_location = close_location.fillna(0.5)
    safe_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0, np.nan)
    volume_base = safe_volume.rolling(19, min_periods=5).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    volume_surprise = (safe_volume / volume_base).clip(0.25, 4.0).fillna(1.0)
    negative_event = -innovation.clip(upper=0.0) * (1.0 - close_location) * volume_surprise
    positive_event = innovation.clip(lower=0.0) * close_location * volume_surprise
    negative_memory = negative_event.ewm(halflife=6, adjust=False, min_periods=1).mean()
    positive_memory = positive_event.ewm(halflife=6, adjust=False, min_periods=1).mean()
    return (negative_memory - positive_memory).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

def _financial_fragility(cash_ratio: pd.DataFrame, current_ratio: pd.DataFrame, debt_to_equity: pd.DataFrame, income_quality: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional balance-sheet fragility in [0, 1]."""
    weak_cash = 1.0 - rank(cash_ratio.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)).fillna(0.5)
    weak_current = 1.0 - rank(current_ratio.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)).fillna(0.5)
    high_debt = rank(debt_to_equity.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)).fillna(0.5)
    weak_cashflow_quality = 1.0 - rank(income_quality.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)).fillna(0.5)
    return (weak_cash + weak_current + high_debt + weak_cashflow_quality) / 4.0

@register_factor
class SignedTailMemoryBalanceBuffer(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks persistent downside tail flow amplified by financial fragility."""
    factor_id = 'signed_tail_memory_balancebuffer_j_1_j_j'
    name = 'Balance-Buffered Downside Tail Memory'
    category = 'volatility'
    description = 'Exponentially decayed negative-minus-positive standardized return-tail memory, weighted by close location and volume surprise, then amplified for weak liquidity, high leverage, and poor cash-flow quality.'
    window_length = 20
    inputs = ['close', 'high', 'low', 'volume', 'cashRatio', 'currentRatio', 'debtToEquity', 'incomeQuality']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        tail_memory = _tail_excitation_imbalance(close, data['high'], data['low'], data['volume'])
        fragility = _financial_fragility(data['cashRatio'], data['currentRatio'], data['debtToEquity'], data['incomeQuality'])
        bearish_score = tail_memory * (1.0 + fragility)
        return rank(bearish_score).fillna(0.5)

A superlinear downside-variance innovation combined with continued negative close-location pressure should predict additional forced selling, whereas an equally extreme shock whose variance acceleration has already rolled over should indicate exhaustion and rebound. The opposite side of the trade is volatility-targeting, risk-parity, and stop-loss capital that mechanically reduces exposure as realized downside risk rises. The mechanism is falsified if the nonlinear variance state has no incremental directional effect after conditioning on the current return and volume surprise."""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

def _downside_semivariance(ret: pd.DataFrame, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal trailing mean of squared negative returns."""
    downside_squared = ret.where(ret < 0.0, 0.0).pow(2)
    return downside_squared.rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()

def _convex_variance_acceleration(ret: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Measure acceleration of a superlinear downside-variance innovation.

    Short downside semivariance is compared with a slower realized-risk regime.
    Squaring only positive innovations makes unusually rapid downside-risk
    expansion materially larger than ordinary variation.  Differencing this
    state at a positive lag distinguishes active deleveraging from relaxation.
    """
    short_semivar = _downside_semivariance(ret, 8)
    baseline_semivar = _downside_semivariance(ret, 40)
    variance_ratio = short_semivar / baseline_semivar.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    innovation = np.log(variance_ratio).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    innovation = innovation.clip(lower=-2.0, upper=2.0).fillna(0.0)
    positive_innovation = innovation.clip(lower=0.0)
    convex_state = positive_innovation.pow(2)
    return (convex_state - convex_state.shift(3)).fillna(0.0)

Accelerating stress receives negative scores while decaying stress receives positive rebound scores.'
    window_length = 60

        low = data['low']
        volume = data['volume'].clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)
        ret = close.pct_change(fill_method=None).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        ret = ret.fillna(0.0)
        variance_acceleration = _convex_variance_acceleration(ret)
        price_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        close_location = (2.0 * close - high - low) / price_range
        close_location = close_location.clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.0)
        signed_close_location_return = close_location * ret.abs()
        volume_baseline = volume.rolling(34, min_periods=10).mean()

        abnormal_volume_amplitude = (1.0 + volume_excess).fillna(1.0)
        raw_signal = variance_acceleration * signed_close_location_return * abnormal_volume_amplitude
        raw_signal = raw_signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        return (rank(raw_signal) - 0.5).fillna(0.0)

Large signed volume with unusually poor close retention is consistent with temporary liquidity pressure, dealer inventory transfer, or a one-sided execution program rather than durable information, creating a short-horizon reversal opportunity. Conversely, high-volume moves that close near the extreme and exceed the stock's historically estimated permanent-impact response are more likely to continue. The hypothesis is rejected if close-retention-adjusted impact residuals do not predict subsequent returns after controlling for ordinary return, range, and volume effects."""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _rolling_permanent_impact(signed_flow: pd.DataFrame, displacement: pd.DataFrame, window: int, min_periods: int) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Estimate a prior-sample rolling OLS permanent-impact response.

    The coefficient at t is fit only through t-1, then applied to current
    signed flow.  This avoids allowing the current bar to mechanically set
    its own expected impact.
    """
    prior_flow = signed_flow.shift(1)
    prior_move = displacement.shift(1)
    mean_flow = prior_flow.rolling(window, min_periods=min_periods).mean()
    mean_move = prior_move.rolling(window, min_periods=min_periods).mean()
    mean_cross = (prior_flow * prior_move).rolling(window, min_periods=min_periods).mean()
    mean_square = (prior_flow * prior_flow).rolling(window, min_periods=min_periods).mean()
    covariance = mean_cross - mean_flow * mean_move
    variance = mean_square - mean_flow * mean_flow
    beta = covariance / variance.where(variance.abs() > 1e-12)
    beta = beta.clip(-0.1, 0.1)
    intercept = mean_move - beta * mean_flow
    expected = intercept + beta * signed_flow
    residual = displacement - expected
    return (expected, residual)

def _impact_dislocation_score(open_: pd.DataFrame, high: pd.DataFrame, low: pd.DataFrame, close: pd.DataFrame, volume: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:

    prior_close = close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)

    bar_range = (high - low).clip(lower=0.0)
    safe_range = bar_range.where(bar_range > 0.0)
    close_location = ((2.0 * close - high - low) / safe_range).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
    close_location = close_location.fillna(0.0)
    clean_volume = volume.clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)
    prior_adv = clean_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean()
    flow_scale = prior_adv.where(prior_adv > 0.0)
    signed_flow = (close_location * clean_volume / flow_scale).clip(-5.0, 5.0)
    signed_flow = signed_flow.fillna(0.0)
    expected, residual = _rolling_permanent_impact(signed_flow, displacement, 60, 40)
    retention = ((close - open_).abs() / safe_range).clip(0.0, 1.0).fillna(0.0)
    range_fraction = (bar_range / prior_close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
    prior_range = range_fraction.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean()
    range_multiple = (range_fraction / prior_range.where(prior_range > 0.0)).clip(0.0, 5.0).fillna(1.0)
    volume_multiple = (clean_volume / flow_scale).clip(0.0, 5.0).fillna(0.0)
    pressure_activity = np.sqrt(range_multiple * volume_multiple).clip(0.0, 5.0)
    prior_residual_scale = residual.shift(1).rolling(23, min_periods=10).std()
    fallback_scale = displacement.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).std()
    scale = prior_residual_scale.where(prior_residual_scale > 1e-06, fallback_scale)

    temporary_pressure = (1.0 - retention) * pressure_activity * displacement / scale
    score = permanent_gap + retained_impact - temporary_pressure
    return score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-12.0, 12.0)

"""Downward return shocks accompanied by unusually large ranges and volume can self-excite through margin calls, volatility targeting, and dealer risk reduction. The signal seeks stocks with a large accumulated downside-excitation state but declining marginal shock marks, indicating that forced selling remains visible in the price path while its incremental intensity is cooling; these names should rebound over the next week. The opposite configuration after an upside cascade is shorted, and the mechanism is rejected if excitation remains proportional rather than saturating and cooling states do not reverse more than equally severe active cascades."""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _trailing_zscore(values: pd.DataFrame, window: int, min_periods: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal rolling standardisation, guarded against flat histories."""
    mean = values.rolling(window, min_periods=min_periods).mean()
    std = values.rolling(window, min_periods=min_periods).std()
    zscore = (values - mean) / std.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return zscore.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

def _marked_aftershock_gap(close: pd.DataFrame, high: pd.DataFrame, low: pd.DataFrame, volume: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Estimate signed Hawkes-like aftershock saturation from causal marks.

    A slow exponentially decayed excitation state represents accumulated prior
    shocks.  A faster state represents marginal current excitation.  Their
    difference is positive only when an existing cascade is cooling rather
    than when shocks continue proportionally at their recent rate.
    """
    safe_close = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    ret = close.pct_change(fill_method=None).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    ret = ret.fillna(0.0)
    intraday_range = ((high - low).abs() / safe_close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    intraday_range = intraday_range.fillna(0.0)
    log_volume = np.log1p(volume.where(volume > 0.0, 0.0).fillna(0.0))
    range_surprise = _trailing_zscore(intraday_range, 20, 10).fillna(0.0)
    volume_surprise = _trailing_zscore(log_volume, 20, 10).fillna(0.0)
    mark = (1.0 + range_surprise.clip(lower=0.0)) * (1.0 + volume_surprise.clip(lower=0.0))
    return_vol = ret.rolling(17, min_periods=10).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    standardized_move = (ret.abs() / return_vol).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    shock_excess = (standardized_move - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)
    downside_events = shock_excess.where(ret < 0.0, 0.0) * mark
    upside_events = shock_excess.where(ret > 0.0, 0.0) * mark
    slow_alpha = 1.0 - np.exp(np.log(0.5) / 5.0)
    fast_alpha = 1.0 - np.exp(np.log(0.5) / 1.0)
    downside_slow = downside_events.ewm(alpha=slow_alpha, adjust=False, min_periods=10).mean()
    downside_fast = downside_events.ewm(alpha=fast_alpha, adjust=False, min_periods=10).mean()
    upside_slow = upside_events.ewm(alpha=slow_alpha, adjust=False, min_periods=10).mean()
    upside_fast = upside_events.ewm(alpha=fast_alpha, adjust=False, min_periods=10).mean()
    downside_cooling = downside_slow - downside_fast
    upside_cooling = upside_slow - upside_fast
    return (downside_cooling - upside_cooling).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

    """Long cooling downside cascades and short cooling upside cascades."""
    factor_id = 'crash_aftershock_convexity_gap_j_1_j'
    name = 'Downside Aftershock Saturation Reversal'
    category = 'mean_reversion'
    description = 'Build a causal, exponentially decayed marked-event intensity from negative and positive daily return shocks, where each event mark combines standardized intraday range and volume surprise. Score the divergence between cumulative same-sign excitation and the most recent marginal excitation, with the factor positive for exhausted downside cascades and negative for exhausted upside cascades.'
    window_length = 40
    inputs = ['close', 'high', 'low', 'volume']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        raw_gap = _marked_aftershock_gap(data['close'], data['high'], data['low'], data['volume'])
        return rank(raw_gap).fillna(0.5) - 0.5

def _rolling_permanent_impact(signed_flow: pd.DataFrame, displacement: pd.DataFrame, window: int, min_periods: int) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Estimate a prior-sample rolling OLS permanent-impact response.

    The coefficient at t is fit only through t-1, then applied to current
    signed flow.  This avoids allowing the current bar to mechanically set
    its own expected impact.
    """
    prior_flow = signed_flow.shift(1)
    prior_move = displacement.shift(1)
    mean_flow = prior_flow.rolling(window, min_periods=min_periods).mean()
    mean_move = prior_move.rolling(window, min_periods=min_periods).mean()
    mean_cross = (prior_flow * prior_move).rolling(window, min_periods=min_periods).mean()
    mean_square = (prior_flow * prior_flow).rolling(window, min_periods=min_periods).mean()
    covariance = mean_cross - mean_flow * mean_move
    variance = mean_square - mean_flow * mean_flow
    beta = covariance / variance.where(variance.abs() > 1e-12)
    beta = beta.clip(-0.1, 0.1)

    expected = intercept + beta * signed_flow
    residual = displacement - expected
    return (expected, residual)

"""An opening gap is more informative when the market absorbs attempted intraday reversal without retracing the gap, particularly on unusually high participation. This is a daily-bar proxy for an opening liquidity shock in which one side of the book is depleted and subsequent limit-order replenishment is insufficient to reverse the information-driven move. The hypothesis is falsified if gap-resilient names reverse over the next six bars after sector adjustment; the opposite side is likely supplied by opening-auction liquidity providers and discretionary traders anchored to the prior close."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import indneutralize, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _gap_resilience_score(
    open_: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal daily proxy for gap retention after an opening depth shock.

    A signed gap is scaled by prior close.  Its retention is measured from the
    open through the closing price, while the adverse excursion measures how
    far price travelled against the opening displacement.  Volume is compared
    with a trailing 20-bar baseline, so high-participation resilient gaps get
    more weight.  All references use the current or earlier bar only.
    """
    prior_close = close.shift(1)
    safe_prior_close = prior_close.replace(0.0, np.nan)

    signed_gap = (open_ - prior_close) / safe_prior_close
    gap_size = signed_gap.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    direction = np.sign(signed_gap)

    close_move_from_open = (close - open_) / safe_prior_close
    retained_fraction = direction * close_move_from_open / gap_size

    adverse_move = pd.DataFrame(
        np.where(
            direction.to_numpy() >= 0.0,
            ((open_ - low) / safe_prior_close).to_numpy(),
            ((high - open_) / safe_prior_close).to_numpy(),
        ),
        index=close.index,
        columns=close.columns,
    )
    retracement_fraction = adverse_move / gap_size

    # Cap extremes caused by tiny price denominators or stale/erroneous bars.
    retained_fraction = retained_fraction.clip(lower=-2.0, upper=2.0)
    retracement_fraction = retracement_fraction.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)

    volume_baseline = volume.rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    relative_volume = volume / volume_baseline
    participation = np.log1p(relative_volume.clip(lower=0.0, upper=10.0)) / np.log(2.0)
    participation = participation.clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0)

    # A close beyond the gap direction is evidence of sustained depletion;
    # adverse intraday movement represents successful opposing liquidity supply.
    resilience = retained_fraction - retracement_fraction
    score = direction * gap_size * resilience * participation
    return score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


@register_factor
class GapResilienceDepthDepletionDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks sector-adjusted, high-participation opening gaps that resist reversal."""

    factor_id = "gap_resilience_depth_depletion_drift"
    name = "Opening Gap Resilience Under Depth Depletion"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Sector-adjusted cross-sectional rank of signed opening gaps that retain "
        "their displacement through the close on abnormal volume, penalizing "
        "intraday movement against the gap direction."
    )
    window_length = 20
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        score = _gap_resilience_score(
            data["open"],
            data["high"],
            data["low"],
            close,
            data["volume"],
        )
        sector_adjusted = indneutralize(score, data["sector"])
        return rank(sector_adjusted).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

"""Daily range per unit of volume is an imperfect but useful revealed-depth measure: when a modest directional flow shock suddenly creates an outsized range, displayed and latent liquidity are likely failing to replenish. Unlike a generic volatility signal, the factor requires directional close-location confirmation and compares current impact elasticity with the name's own recent elasticity state. It should be rejected if these elasticity breaks merely forecast symmetric volatility rather than signed continuation; the inefficiency persists because market makers widen or withdraw after the shock while slower capital needs several sessions to restore inventory and depth."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _robust_elasticity_innovation(
    elasticity: pd.DataFrame, baseline_window: int, scale_window: int
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal robust surprise in range-per-volume elasticity.

    The rolling median defines the normal revealed-depth state.  A trailing
    median absolute deviation (MAD) supplies a robust scale, making a single
    extreme range less likely to redefine the baseline immediately.
    """
    baseline = elasticity.rolling(
        baseline_window, min_periods=baseline_window
    ).median()
    deviation = (elasticity - baseline).abs()
    mad = deviation.rolling(scale_window, min_periods=scale_window).median()
    robust_scale = (1.4826 * mad).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    innovation = (elasticity - baseline) / robust_scale
    return innovation.clip(lower=-8.0, upper=8.0)


@register_factor
class LiquidityReplenishmentFailure(BaseFactor):
    """Directional revealed-depth breaks caused by failed liquidity replenishment."""

    factor_id = "range_elasticity_replenishment_failure"
    name = "Liquidity Replenishment Failure"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional rank of a signed, robust range-per-volume elasticity "
        "shock: long upside close-location depletion and short downside "
        "close-location depletion after revealed depth fails to replenish."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["high", "low", "close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        high = data["high"].astype(float)
        low = data["low"].astype(float)
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float)

        bar_range = (high - low).clip(lower=0.0)
        safe_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0, np.nan)

        # Log scaling prevents nominal share-volume differences from dominating
        # the proxy while preserving the inverse relation between depth and range.
        elasticity = bar_range / np.log1p(safe_volume)
        elasticity = elasticity.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        innovation = _robust_elasticity_innovation(elasticity, 40, 20)

        # Close location is in [-1, 1]: a range ending near its high (low)
        # identifies upward (downward) directional flow behind the depletion.
        safe_range = bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        close_location = ((2.0 * close - high - low) / safe_range).clip(
            lower=-1.0, upper=1.0
        )
        close_location = close_location.fillna(0.0)

        directional_depletion = (innovation * close_location).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )
        signal = rank(directional_depletion)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

"""An opening gap that remains accepted through the close despite unusually large range per unit volume is consistent with liquidity having been withdrawn near the opening and informed demand exhausting the available displayed depth. Unlike a mechanically induced opening gap that refills rapidly, accepted gaps in a thin execution environment should continue while market makers rebuild inventory and stale limit orders are repriced. The idea is rejected if these accepted thin-book gaps mean-revert more strongly than equally sized, high-participation gaps."""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _finite(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Mask non-finite observations without manufacturing price information."""
    return frame.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

def _cross_sectional_zscore(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Daily cross-sectional standardization with safe treatment of sparse rows."""
    clean = _finite(frame)
    row_mean = clean.mean(axis=1)
    row_std = clean.std(axis=1, ddof=0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    zscore = clean.sub(row_mean, axis=0).div(row_std, axis=0)

"""Institutional execution programs often split a parent order into repeated slices whose timing is constrained by participation targets, benchmark schedules, and risk limits. A coherent periodic signed-volume pattern with a projected next slice in the same direction should indicate unfinished metaorder demand and continued short-horizon price pressure. The hypothesis is falsified if high spectral concentration in signed participation does not predict same-sign future returns after controlling for recent return and relative volume."""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _spectral_projection(flow: pd.DataFrame, window: int, horizon: int) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Project the strongest short-cycle Fourier component forward causally.

    Each trailing window is demeaned before its discrete Fourier coefficients
    are evaluated at execution-like periods.  The selected component is then
    reconstructed at ``horizon`` bars after the current endpoint.  Coherence
    is the selected harmonic's share of trailing flow energy.
    """
    values = flow.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=True)
    n_rows, n_cols = values.shape
    projected = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    coherence = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    if n_rows < window:
        return (pd.DataFrame(projected, index=flow.index, columns=flow.columns), pd.DataFrame(coherence, index=flow.index, columns=flow.columns))
    values = np.nan_to_num(values, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
    trailing = np.lib.stride_tricks.sliding_window_view(values, window_shape=window, axis=0)
    centered = trailing - trailing.mean(axis=2, keepdims=True)
    periods = np.array([4.0, 6.0, 8.0, 12.0], dtype=float)
    positions = np.arange(window, dtype=float)
    frequencies = 2.0 * np.pi / periods
    basis = np.exp(-1j * frequencies[:, None] * positions[None, :])
    coefficients = np.einsum('tnw,kw->tnk', centered, basis)
    power = coefficients.real * coefficients.real + coefficients.imag * coefficients.imag
    best = np.argmax(power, axis=2)
    selected_power = np.take_along_axis(power, best[..., None], axis=2)[..., 0]
    selected_coeff = np.take_along_axis(coefficients, best[..., None], axis=2)[..., 0]
    selected_frequency = frequencies[best]
    energy = np.sum(centered * centered, axis=2)
    selected_coherence = 2.0 * selected_power / (window * energy + 1e-12)
    selected_coherence = np.clip(selected_coherence, 0.0, 1.0)
    future_position = float(window - 1 + horizon)
    future_phase = np.exp(1j * selected_frequency * future_position)
    selected_projection = 2.0 / window * np.real(selected_coeff * future_phase)
    projected[window - 1:] = selected_projection
    coherence[window - 1:] = selected_coherence
    return (pd.DataFrame(projected, index=flow.index, columns=flow.columns), pd.DataFrame(coherence, index=flow.index, columns=flow.columns))

def _rolling_flow_residual(signal_df: pd.DataFrame, recent_return: pd.DataFrame, relative_volume: pd.DataFrame, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing multiple-OLS residual of projected flow on return and volume."""
    y = signal_df.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=True)
    ret = recent_return.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=True)
    vol = relative_volume.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=True)
    n_rows, n_cols = y.shape
    residual = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    if n_rows < window:
        return pd.DataFrame(residual, index=signal_df.index, columns=signal_df.columns)
    valid = np.isfinite(y) & np.isfinite(ret) & np.isfinite(vol)
    y = np.nan_to_num(y, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
    ret = np.nan_to_num(ret, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
    vol = np.nan_to_num(vol, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
    yw = np.lib.stride_tricks.sliding_window_view(y, window_shape=window, axis=0)
    rw = np.lib.stride_tricks.sliding_window_view(ret, window_shape=window, axis=0)
    vw = np.lib.stride_tricks.sliding_window_view(vol, window_shape=window, axis=0)
    mw = np.lib.stride_tricks.sliding_window_view(valid, window_shape=window, axis=0)
    weights = mw.astype(float)
    design = np.stack([np.ones_like(rw), rw, vw], axis=3) * weights[..., None]
    weighted_y = yw * weights
    xtx = np.einsum('tnwi,tnwj->tnij', design, design)
    xty = np.einsum('tnwi,tnw->tni', design, weighted_y)
    with np.errstate(all='ignore'):
        beta = np.einsum('tnij,tnj->tni', np.linalg.pinv(xtx), xty)
    current_fit = beta[..., 0] + beta[..., 1] * ret[window - 1:] + beta[..., 2] * vol[window - 1:]
    current_residual = y[window - 1:] - current_fit
    enough_observations = mw.sum(axis=2) >= max(12, window // 2)
    residual[window - 1:] = np.where(enough_observations, current_residual, np.nan)
    return pd.DataFrame(residual, index=signal_df.index, columns=signal_df.columns)

class SpectralExecutionCadenceResidualDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Fourier-projected residual signed participation for unfinished execution demand."""
    factor_id = 'spectral_execution_cadence_residual_drift_j_j_1__1'
    name = 'Spectral Execution Cadence Drift'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = 'Ranks a six-bar Fourier phase projection of close-location signed participation after residualizing it against recent return and relative volume, with spectral coherence and range efficiency weights.'
    window_length = 64
    inputs = ['close', 'high', 'low', 'volume']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].astype(float)
        high = data['high'].astype(float)
        low = data['low'].astype(float)
        volume = data['volume'].astype(float).fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        safe_close = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        bar_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        close_location = ((2.0 * close - high - low) / bar_range).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        close_location = close_location.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        volume_base = volume.rolling(19, min_periods=10).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        relative_volume = (volume / volume_base).clip(0.0, 5.0)
        relative_volume = relative_volume.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        signed_participation = close_location * relative_volume
        projected_flow, coherence = _spectral_projection(signed_participation, window=32, horizon=6)
        one_bar_return = safe_close / safe_close.shift(1) - 1.0
        recent_return = safe_close / safe_close.shift(7) - 1.0
        recent_return = recent_return.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        residual_flow = _rolling_flow_residual(projected_flow, recent_return, relative_volume, window=32)
        normalized_range = ((high - low).abs() / safe_close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        gross_range = normalized_range.rolling(9, min_periods=4).sum().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        net_move = recent_return.abs()
        range_efficiency = (net_move / gross_range).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        range_efficiency = range_efficiency.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        raw_signal = residual_flow * coherence * range_efficiency
        raw_signal = raw_signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        return rank(raw_signal).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

"""Stocks with large negative return sensitivity to market-wide depth deterioration should underperform when a new aggregate liquidity shock arrives, because leveraged and inventory-constrained intermediaries reduce those exposures first. The other side is slow-moving capital or liquidity providers unable to immediately warehouse correlated liquidity risk, allowing the liquidation premium to persist for several sessions. The hypothesis is falsified if high tail-liquidity-loading names do not have materially worse six-day returns than low-loading names specifically following broad depth deterioration, after sector and size controls."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _aggregate_liquidity_stress(
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
) -> pd.Series:
    """Causal standardized shock in median cross-sectional price impact."""
    safe_close = close.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    dollar_volume = (safe_close * volume.abs()).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    normalized_range = (high - low).clip(lower=0.0) / safe_close
    illiquidity = (normalized_range / dollar_volume).replace(
        [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
    )

    market_illiquidity = illiquidity.median(axis=1, skipna=True).replace(
        [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
    )
    baseline = market_illiquidity.rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    dispersion = market_illiquidity.rolling(window, min_periods=window).std()
    shock = (market_illiquidity - baseline) / dispersion.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return shock.clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _positive_stress_beta(
    stock_returns: pd.DataFrame,
    stress: pd.Series,
    window: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing OLS slope of returns on positive aggregate stress shocks.

    The regression is estimated only on positive stress observations.  This is
    a causal downside beta: at each date all sufficient statistics use the
    current and preceding observations only.
    """
    stress_panel = pd.DataFrame(
        np.tile(stress.to_numpy()[:, None], (1, stock_returns.shape[1])),
        index=stock_returns.index,
        columns=stock_returns.columns,
    )
    event = stress_panel.gt(0.0) & stress_panel.notna() & stock_returns.notna()
    weight = event.astype(float)
    x = stress_panel.where(event, 0.0)
    y = stock_returns.where(event, 0.0)

    rolling = lambda frame: frame.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    count = rolling(weight)
    sum_x = rolling(x)
    sum_y = rolling(y)
    sum_xx = rolling(x * x)
    sum_xy = rolling(x * y)

    denominator = count * sum_xx - sum_x * sum_x
    beta = (count * sum_xy - sum_x * sum_y) / denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    minimum_events = max(20, window // 6)
    return beta.where(count >= minimum_events).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


@register_factor
class TailLiquidityLoadingStateSpread(BaseFactor):
    """Bearish state-dependent loading on broad liquidity deterioration."""

    factor_id = "tail_liquidity_loading_state_spread"
    name = "Tail Liquidity-Loading Deleveraging Spread"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks the negative of each stock's trailing return beta to positive "
        "aggregate liquidity-stress shocks, interacted with the current shock; "
        "high loading names receive bearish scores because constrained "
        "intermediaries deleverage them first during broad depth deterioration."
    )
    window_length = 180
    inputs = ["high", "low", "close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        stock_returns = (close / close.shift(1) - 1.0).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )
        stress = _aggregate_liquidity_stress(
            data["high"], data["low"], close, data["volume"], 60
        )
        beta = _positive_stress_beta(stock_returns, stress, 180)

        # A negative beta is a positive deleveraging loading: the stock falls
        # when aggregate liquidity deteriorates.  The current state activates
        # that loading; negative output is intentionally bearish for high risk.
        loading = -beta
        state_score = loading.mul(stress, axis=0)
        bearish_rank = state_score.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        return (0.5 - bearish_rank).fillna(0.0)

"""A fresh quarterly change in net stock issuance or share-count growth identifies a public corporate-equity-supply shock, but its informational content depends on whether the market can absorb it. Positive issuance accompanied by a positive availability-day price response reveals demand strong enough to overcome expected dilution pressure; conversely, price weakness despite a repurchase or shrinking share count reveals latent selling stronger than corporate demand. Slow-moving capital, underwriting inventory, and investors who mechanically trade the disclosed capital-action headline can leave this relative-demand information incompletely incorporated over the following week."""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _fresh_observation(field: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Flag a newly available quarterly value or a material PIT step change."""
    previous = field.shift(1)
    tolerance = 1e-12 + 1e-08 * previous.abs()
    changed = (field - previous).abs() > tolerance
    first_available = field.notna() & previous.isna()
    return changed.fillna(False) | first_available

def _absorption_alignment(close: pd.DataFrame, volume: pd.DataFrame, supply: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Return causal signed return and volume-surprise agreement with supply.

    Both normalizers exclude the current bar from their reference samples.  A
    positive supply shock therefore needs a positive return and positive volume
    surprise, while a negative supply shock needs both measures to be negative.
    """
    ret = close.pct_change()
    ret_scale = ret.shift(1).rolling(23, min_periods=15).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return_z = ret / ret_scale
    valid_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0)
    log_volume = np.log1p(valid_volume)
    volume_mean = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(18, min_periods=15).mean()
    volume_std = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(23, min_periods=15).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    volume_z = (log_volume - volume_mean) / volume_std
    supply_sign = np.sign(supply)
    return_agreement = (supply_sign * np.tanh(return_z)).clip(lower=0.0)
    volume_agreement = (supply_sign * np.tanh(volume_z)).clip(lower=0.0)
    return (return_agreement, volume_agreement)

class DisclosureSupplyAbsorptionAsymmetry(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks fresh corporate supply disclosures by contemporaneous market absorption."""

    window_length = 21
    inputs = ['close', 'volume', 'marketCap', 'netStockIssuance', 'sharesGrowth']

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        volume = data['volume']
        market_cap = data['marketCap'].where(data['marketCap'] > 0.0)

"""The insider-purchase paper argues that price strength near a prior high can be confirmation of slowly incorporated information rather than an exhausted trend, especially in smaller and less liquid names. This factor isolates a ratchet-shaped discovery process: repeated approaches to the rolling high with progressively shallower pullbacks, rather than a single high-return momentum observation. The other side is liquidity suppliers and valuation-constrained investors who repeatedly sell at the prior high; the hypothesis is falsified if these compressed pullbacks do not predict positive six-day continuation after controlling for ordinary return momentum."""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _highwater_ratchet(close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causally score repeated high-water reclamation and improving pullbacks."""
    highwater = close.rolling(260, min_periods=126).max().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    drawdown = (1.0 - close / highwater).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
    near_high = (close / highwater >= 0.985).astype(float)
    near_high = near_high.where(close.notna() & highwater.notna())
    reclaim_frequency = near_high.rolling(143, min_periods=84).mean()
    recent_depth = drawdown.rolling(68, min_periods=42).mean()
    prior_depth = drawdown.shift(62).rolling(68, min_periods=42).mean()
    compression = (prior_depth - recent_depth) / (prior_depth + 0.01)
    compression = compression.clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0)
    shallowness = (1.0 - recent_depth).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
    return reclaim_frequency * shallowness * compression

@register_factor
class HighwaterLiquidityRatchetDrift(BaseFactor):
    """High-water reclamation with compressed pullbacks in capacity-constrained names."""
    factor_id = 'highwater_liquidity_ratchet_drift_j_3_j_j_j_1'
    name = 'Illiquid High-Water Ratchet Drift'
    category = 'momentum'
    description = 'Ranks a causal high-water ratchet score: frequent closes near a 252-bar high combined with progressively shallower 63-bar pullbacks, weighted toward small, low-dollar-capacity names while penalizing climactic volume.'
    window_length = 252
    inputs = ['close', 'volume', 'marketCap']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        volume = data['volume'].abs()
        market_cap = data['marketCap']
        ratchet = _highwater_ratchet(close)
        dollar_volume = close.abs() * volume
        dollar_capacity = dollar_volume.rolling(16, min_periods=10).mean()
        capacity_rank = rank(np.log(dollar_capacity.replace(0.0, np.nan))).fillna(0.5)
        low_capacity_weight = 1.25 - capacity_rank
        size_rank = rank(np.log(market_cap.where(market_cap > 0.0))).fillna(0.5)
        small_cap_weight = 1.25 - size_rank
        short_volume = dollar_volume.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()
        normal_volume = dollar_volume.rolling(74, min_periods=30).mean()
        relative_volume = (short_volume / normal_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)).fillna(1.0)
        climactic_excess = (relative_volume - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        modest_volume_weight = np.exp(-2.0 * climactic_excess)
        score = ratchet * low_capacity_weight * small_cap_weight * modest_volume_weight
        valid = ratchet.notna()
        return rank(score.where(valid)).fillna(0.0)

Investors who process filings slowly and liquidity providers reluctant to absorb potential future supply create a delayed negative repricing, especially when the initial price response is muted. The idea fails if fresh funding deterioration is fully incorporated on its availability date, leaving no incremental six-day underperformance among low-capacity names."""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _fresh_change(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return a change only on a genuine new point-in-time disclosure."""
    prior = df.shift(1)
    changed = df.notna() & prior.notna() & df.ne(prior)
    return (df - prior).where(changed)

def _robust_cross_sectional_zscore(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal row-wise robust standardisation using contemporaneous peers."""
    median = df.median(axis=1)
    deviation = df.sub(median, axis=0).abs()
    mad = deviation.median(axis=1)
    robust_scale = 1.4826 * mad
    fallback_scale = df.std(axis=1)
    scale = robust_scale.where(robust_scale > 1e-12, fallback_scale)
    scale = scale.where(scale > 1e-12)
    zscore = df.sub(median, axis=0).div(scale, axis=0)
    return zscore.clip(-4.0, 4.0)

def _event_decay(events: pd.DataFrame, half_life: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Propagate a filing event forward with a causal exponential decay."""
    alpha = 1.0 - np.exp(np.log(0.5) / half_life)
    return events.fillna(0.0).ewm(alpha=alpha, adjust=False).mean()

class FreshFundingGapAbsorptionDelay(BaseFactor):
    """Funding deterioration delayed by weak trading absorption."""
    factor_id = 'fresh_funding_gap_absorption_delay_j_j_j_4'
    name = 'Fresh Funding-Gap Absorption Delay'
    category = 'other'
    description = 'Ranks firms by the negative of a fresh funding-gap deterioration event that is amplified when recent dollar trading capacity is low and the contemporaneous price response is muted.'
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ['close', 'volume', 'marketCap', 'cashConversionCycle', 'shortTermDebt', 'cash', 'changeInWorkingCapital']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        volume = data['volume']
        market_cap = data['marketCap']
        cash_conversion_cycle = data['cashConversionCycle']
        short_term_debt = data['shortTermDebt']
        cash = data['cash']
        working_capital_change = data['changeInWorkingCapital']
        safe_market_cap = market_cap.where(market_cap > 0.0)
        ccc_prior = cash_conversion_cycle.shift(1).abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ccc_deterioration = _fresh_change(cash_conversion_cycle).div(ccc_prior)
        debt_cash_deterioration = (_fresh_change(short_term_debt) - _fresh_change(cash)).div(safe_market_cap)
        working_capital_deterioration = -_fresh_change(working_capital_change).div(safe_market_cap)
        components = [_robust_cross_sectional_zscore(ccc_deterioration), _robust_cross_sectional_zscore(debt_cash_deterioration), _robust_cross_sectional_zscore(working_capital_deterioration)]
        available = sum((component.notna().astype(float) for component in components))
        funding_score = sum((component.fillna(0.0) for component in components)).div(available.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        dollar_volume = (close * volume).where((close > 0.0) & (volume > 0.0))
        short_dollar_volume = dollar_volume.rolling(4, min_periods=3).mean()
        baseline_dollar_volume = dollar_volume.rolling(47, min_periods=10).mean()
        low_capacity = (1.0 - short_dollar_volume.div(baseline_dollar_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan))).clip(0.0, 1.0).fillna(0.0)
        ret = returns(data)
        daily_volatility = ret.rolling(21, min_periods=10).std()
        reaction_size = ret.abs().div(daily_volatility.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        muted_reaction = (1.0 - reaction_size).clip(0.0, 1.0).fillna(0.0)
        absorption_penalty = 1.0 + low_capacity + muted_reaction
        delayed_hazard = _event_decay(funding_score * absorption_penalty, 3.0)
        return rank(-delayed_hazard).fillna(0.5)

"""Daily signed return-volume shocks can proxy clustered informed order flow even when message-level order data are unavailable. A self-exciting flow episode should continue when its estimated branching intensity is elevated but still subcritical; once intensity is near saturation, liquidity-provider inventory and late follower exhaustion make reversal more likely. The hypothesis is falsified if moderate estimated self-excitation has no more positive six-day continuation than isolated shocks, or if only saturated cascades continue."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _hawkes_states(
    events: pd.DataFrame, decay: float
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Causally accumulate signed and absolute exponential event kernels."""
    values = events.fillna(0.0).to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=True)
    n_rows, n_cols = values.shape
    signed_state = np.zeros((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=float)
    absolute_state = np.zeros((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=float)
    prior_absolute = np.zeros((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=float)

    signed_running = np.zeros(n_cols, dtype=float)
    absolute_running = np.zeros(n_cols, dtype=float)

    for row in range(n_rows):
        prior_absolute[row] = absolute_running
        signed_running = decay * signed_running + values[row]
        absolute_running = decay * absolute_running + np.abs(values[row])
        signed_state[row] = signed_running
        absolute_state[row] = absolute_running

    return (
        pd.DataFrame(signed_state, index=events.index, columns=events.columns),
        pd.DataFrame(absolute_state, index=events.index, columns=events.columns),
        pd.DataFrame(prior_absolute, index=events.index, columns=events.columns),
    )


def _signed_flow_events(close: pd.DataFrame, volume: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Create bounded directional events from abnormal return-volume marks."""
    ret = close.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
    vol = volume.fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
    typical_vol = vol.rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    relative_vol = (vol / typical_vol).clip(lower=0.0, upper=8.0).fillna(0.0)

    marks = (ret * relative_vol).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
    mark_mean = marks.rolling(40, min_periods=20).mean()
    mark_std = marks.rolling(40, min_periods=20).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    z_mark = ((marks - mark_mean) / mark_std).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

    excess = (z_mark.abs() - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
    return (np.sign(z_mark) * excess).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class SubcriticalSignedFlowCascadeDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks directional Hawkes-like flow intensity only during subcritical cascades."""

    factor_id = "subcritical_signed_flow_cascade_drift"
    name = "Subcritical Signed-Flow Cascade Drift"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Uses abnormal signed return-volume events to form an exponentially "
        "decayed self-exciting flow state. Long-lived directional cascades are "
        "ranked only when the share attributable to prior events is moderate, "
        "excluding isolated shocks and saturated follower flow."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        events = _signed_flow_events(close, volume)

        # Four-bar exponential half-life: daily shocks remain relevant for the
        # six-bar forecast horizon while still distinguishing separate episodes.
        decay = float(np.exp(-np.log(2.0) / 4.0))
        signed_state, absolute_state, prior_absolute = _hawkes_states(events, decay)

        # A slow, strictly prior activity rate is the immigrant/background flow
        # estimate.  The branching proxy measures how much current intensity is
        # inherited from earlier events rather than explained by a new shock.
        background = (
            events.abs()
            .shift(1)
            .ewm(halflife=20.0, adjust=False, min_periods=1)
            .mean()
            .fillna(0.0)
        )
        current_impulse = events.abs()
        branching_proxy = prior_absolute / (
            prior_absolute + current_impulse + background + 1.0e-12
        )

        # Isolated events have near-zero inherited intensity; very high values
        # represent crowded, inventory-sensitive cascades near saturation.
        subcritical = (branching_proxy >= 0.18) & (branching_proxy <= 0.72)
        directional_residual = signed_state / (absolute_state + background + 1.0e-12)
        eligible_signal = directional_residual.where(subcritical)

        return rank(eligible_signal).fillna(0.0)

"""Bubble-driven phase transitions are characterized less by high returns alone than by accelerating trend, shrinking spacing between directional excursions, and increasingly synchronized volume participation. Such paths attract trend-following and performance-chasing capital until marginal buyers are exhausted, at which point a short-horizon reversal becomes likely. The idea fails if accelerating, geometrically compressed price-volume paths remain more persistent than comparable non-compressed trends after controlling for ordinary momentum."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _quadratic_phase_metrics(log_price: pd.DataFrame, window: int) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Causally estimate endpoint slope, aligned quadratic acceleration, and fit quality."""
    values = log_price.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    n_rows, n_cols = values.shape

    slope_out = np.zeros((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=float)
    accel_out = np.zeros((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=float)
    r2_out = np.zeros((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=float)

    # x=0 is the current endpoint, so coefficient b is the endpoint slope.
    x = np.arange(-window + 1, 1, dtype=float)
    design = np.column_stack((np.ones(window), x, x * x))
    projection = np.linalg.pinv(design)

    for end in range(window - 1, n_rows):
        segment = values[end - window + 1 : end + 1]
        valid = np.isfinite(segment).all(axis=0)
        if not np.any(valid):
            continue

        y = segment[:, valid]
        coefficients = projection @ y
        fitted = design @ coefficients
        residual_ss = np.sum((y - fitted) ** 2, axis=0)
        total_ss = np.sum((y - np.mean(y, axis=0, keepdims=True)) ** 2, axis=0)
        fit_quality = 1.0 - residual_ss / np.where(total_ss > 1e-14, total_ss, np.nan)

        slope_out[end, valid] = coefficients[1]
        accel_out[end, valid] = coefficients[2]
        r2_out[end, valid] = np.clip(np.nan_to_num(fit_quality, nan=0.0), 0.0, 1.0)

    return (
        pd.DataFrame(slope_out, index=log_price.index, columns=log_price.columns),
        pd.DataFrame(accel_out, index=log_price.index, columns=log_price.columns),
        pd.DataFrame(r2_out, index=log_price.index, columns=log_price.columns),
    )


def _extrema_compression(log_price: pd.DataFrame, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Measure causal geometric contraction of confirmed directional-excursion intervals."""
    values = log_price.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    n_rows, n_cols = values.shape
    output = np.zeros((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=float)

    for col in range(n_cols):
        series = values[:, col]
        excursion_sign = np.zeros(n_rows, dtype=float)
        last_sign = 0.0
        for t in range(1, n_rows):
            if not (np.isfinite(series[t]) and np.isfinite(series[t - 1])):
                continue
            diff = series[t] - series[t - 1]
            if diff > 0.0:
                last_sign = 1.0
            elif diff < 0.0:
                last_sign = -1.0
            excursion_sign[t] = last_sign

        extrema: list[int] = []
        for t in range(2, n_rows):
            previous = excursion_sign[t - 1]
            current = excursion_sign[t]
            if previous != 0.0 and current != 0.0 and previous != current:
                # The extremum at t-1 is only known after observing return t.
                extrema.append(t - 1)

            if len(extrema) < 4:
                continue

            recent = [point for point in extrema if point >= t - window]
            if len(recent) < 4:
                continue

            intervals = np.diff(np.asarray(recent[-4:], dtype=float))
            if np.any(intervals <= 0.0):
                continue

            # Two successive ratios below one indicate approximately geometric
            # compression; the geometric mean makes the estimate less noisy.
            ratio_1 = intervals[-1] / intervals[-2]
            ratio_2 = intervals[-2] / intervals[-3]
            geometric_ratio = np.sqrt(max(ratio_1 * ratio_2, 0.0))
            contraction = np.clip(1.0 - geometric_ratio, 0.0, 1.0)

            # Compression is most relevant while the latest reversal remains near
            # the endpoint, rather than being a stale historical pattern.
            age = t - recent[-1]
            freshness = np.exp(-age / max(window / 3.0, 1.0))
            output[t, col] = contraction * freshness

    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=log_price.index, columns=log_price.columns)


def _endpoint_volume_concentration(volume: pd.DataFrame, window: int, endpoint: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return a bounded measure of volume concentration in the latest endpoint bars."""
    safe_volume = volume.fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
    endpoint_mean = safe_volume.rolling(endpoint, min_periods=endpoint).mean()
    full_mean = safe_volume.rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    ratio = endpoint_mean / full_mean.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    # A ratio above one means participation is concentrated near the endpoint.
    return ((ratio - 1.0) / 1.5).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class CriticalTimeBubblePhaseInversion(BaseFactor):
    """Contrarian score for volume-confirmed, critically compressed bubble phases."""

    factor_id = "critical_time_bubble_phase_inversion"
    name = "Critical-Time Bubble Phase Inversion"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "Contrarian ranking of accelerating log-price trends whose confirmed "
        "directional excursions contract geometrically and whose trading volume "
        "concentrates near the latest endpoint."
    )
    window_length = 36
    inputs = ["close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        # Forward fill is causal; non-positive observations remain unavailable.
        safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0).ffill()
        log_price = np.log(safe_close)

        slope, acceleration, fit_quality = _quadratic_phase_metrics(log_price, self.window_length)
        compression = _extrema_compression(log_price, self.window_length)
        volume_confirmation = _endpoint_volume_concentration(volume, self.window_length, 4)

        direction = np.sign(slope)
        # A mature critical phase requires acceleration in its prevailing direction.
        aligned_acceleration = (direction * acceleration * (self.window_length ** 2)).clip(lower=0.0)
        acceleration_strength = np.tanh(8.0 * aligned_acceleration)
        trend_strength = np.tanh(3.0 * slope.abs() * self.window_length)

        maturity = (
            trend_strength
            * acceleration_strength
            * fit_quality
            * compression
            * volume_confirmation
        )

        # Upside critical phases are short candidates; downside capitulations are
        # long candidates, hence the inversion of the prevailing trend direction.
        raw_signal = (-direction * maturity).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        return rank(raw_signal).fillna(0.5)

"""The market should process the same earnings or revenue surprise differently depending on whether the issuer has a credible financing buffer. Positive disclosures from cash-rich, low-rollover-risk firms are often underreacted to because investors anchor on stale distress or growth narratives, while negative surprises from debt-dependent firms can trigger a delayed deleveraging cascade. The mechanism is rejected if buffer strength does not systematically increase post-surprise drift asymmetry after accounting for the initial price response."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _fresh_standardized_innovation(
    surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    lookback: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal standardized event innovation, nonzero only when PIT data update."""
    raw = surprise.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    changed = raw.ne(raw.shift(1)) & raw.notna() & raw.shift(1).notna()
    first_observation = raw.notna() & raw.shift(1).isna()
    event = changed | first_observation

    trailing_mean = raw.rolling(lookback, min_periods=2).mean()
    trailing_std = raw.rolling(lookback, min_periods=2).std()
    standardized_level = (raw - trailing_mean) / trailing_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)

    step = raw - raw.shift(1)
    step_scale = step.abs().rolling(lookback, min_periods=2).mean()
    standardized_step = step / step_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)

    innovation = standardized_step.where(changed, standardized_level.where(first_observation, 0.0))
    return innovation.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).where(event, 0.0)


def _event_response_deficit(
    innovation: pd.DataFrame,
    stock_return: pd.DataFrame,
    response_window: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Measure signed disclosure news not yet incorporated in immediate returns.

    The response uses only contemporaneous and prior bar information.  A
    positive value means favorable event news has received less-than-normal
    immediate confirmation; a negative value means adverse news has been
    insufficiently reflected in price.
    """
    response = stock_return.rolling(response_window, min_periods=1).sum()
    response_scale = stock_return.abs().rolling(20, min_periods=5).mean()
    normalized_response = response / response_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    deficit = innovation - normalized_response
    active_event = innovation.ne(0.0)
    return deficit.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).where(active_event, 0.0)


@register_factor
class FinancialBufferedEventResponseDeficit(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks underreacted earnings events by the issuer's financing buffer."""

    factor_id = "financial_buffered_event_response_deficit"
    name = "Financial-Buffer Event Response Deficit"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Combines fresh standardized EPS and revenue surprise innovations with "
        "cash, liquidity, and debt buffers, then ranks the signed gap between "
        "disclosure news and the stock's immediate return response."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "cashRatio",
        "currentRatio",
        "debtToEquity",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"]
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"]
        cash_ratio = data["cashRatio"]
        current_ratio = data["currentRatio"]
        debt_to_equity = data["debtToEquity"]

        eps_event = _fresh_standardized_innovation(eps_surprise, 60)
        revenue_event = _fresh_standardized_innovation(revenue_surprise, 60)

        eps_available = eps_event.ne(0.0)
        revenue_available = revenue_event.ne(0.0)
        event_count = eps_available.astype(float) + revenue_available.astype(float)
        disclosure_innovation = (
            eps_event + revenue_event
        ) / event_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        disclosure_innovation = disclosure_innovation.fillna(0.0)

        cash_component = np.log1p(cash_ratio.clip(lower=0.0)).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )
        liquidity_component = np.log1p(current_ratio.clip(lower=0.0)).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )
        debt_component = np.log1p(debt_to_equity.clip(lower=0.0)).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )

        buffer_raw = cash_component.fillna(0.0) + liquidity_component.fillna(0.0) - debt_component.fillna(0.0)
        buffer_strength = rank(buffer_raw).fillna(0.5) - 0.5

        immediate_return = returns(data).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        response_deficit = _event_response_deficit(
            disclosure_innovation,
            immediate_return,
            2,
        )

        event_direction = np.sign(disclosure_innovation)
        buffer_weight = 1.0 + event_direction * buffer_strength
        signal = response_deficit * buffer_weight
        signal = signal.where(disclosure_innovation.ne(0.0), 0.0)

        return rank(signal).fillna(0.5)

"""Related equities often respond to common sector shocks through a latent correlation network rather than independently. A stock whose recent idiosyncratic return is unusually far from the low-frequency graph-implied return of its correlated sector neighbors can represent a temporary information-diffusion or inventory imbalance, particularly when the sector graph has a stable spectral structure. The other side is sector-basket, ETF, and benchmarked flow that trades the broad shock first while leaving slower names temporarily displaced; the hypothesis is rejected if graph-implied residuals do not converge over the subsequent six sessions after costs."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _build_sector_spectral_model(
    history: np.ndarray,
    candidate_idx: np.ndarray,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, float] | None:
    """Estimate a positive-correlation normalized-Laplacian low-pass model."""
    if candidate_idx.size < 5:
        return None

    panel = history[:, candidate_idx].astype(float, copy=True)
    valid_count = np.isfinite(panel).sum(axis=0)
    enough_history = valid_count >= int(0.90 * panel.shape[0])
    candidate_idx = candidate_idx[enough_history]
    panel = panel[:, enough_history]

    n_names = panel.shape[1]
    if n_names < 5:
        return None

    # Sector demean each historical day before measuring the residual network.
    finite = np.isfinite(panel)
    row_count = finite.sum(axis=1)
    row_sum = np.where(finite, panel, 0.0).sum(axis=1)
    row_mean = np.divide(
        row_sum,
        row_count,
        out=np.zeros_like(row_sum, dtype=float),
        where=row_count > 0,
    )
    residual_panel = panel - row_mean[:, None]

    # Sparse observations are neutral residuals rather than artificial shocks.
    residual_panel = np.where(np.isfinite(residual_panel), residual_panel, 0.0)
    corr = np.corrcoef(residual_panel, rowvar=False)
    if corr.ndim != 2 or corr.shape != (n_names, n_names):
        return None

    corr = np.nan_to_num(corr, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
    adjacency = np.maximum(corr, 0.0)
    np.fill_diagonal(adjacency, 0.0)

    degree = adjacency.sum(axis=1)
    if np.count_nonzero(degree > 1.0e-10) < n_names:
        return None

    inv_sqrt_degree = 1.0 / np.sqrt(degree)
    normalized_adjacency = adjacency * inv_sqrt_degree[:, None] * inv_sqrt_degree[None, :]
    laplacian = np.eye(n_names) - normalized_adjacency

    try:
        eigenvalues, eigenvectors = np.linalg.eigh(laplacian)
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
        return None

    # A small low-frequency basis captures broad residual-sector shocks while
    # retaining an eigengap test for whether that basis is well identified.
    n_modes = min(3, n_names - 2)
    if n_modes < 1 or n_modes >= n_names:
        return None

    eigengap = float(eigenvalues[n_modes] - eigenvalues[n_modes - 1])
    average_edge = float(np.mean(degree) / max(n_names - 1, 1))
    stability = np.clip(eigengap / 0.15, 0.0, 1.0)
    connectivity = np.clip(average_edge / 0.05, 0.0, 1.0)
    confidence = stability * connectivity
    if confidence <= 0.0:
        return None

    low_frequency_vectors = eigenvectors[:, :n_modes]
    smoother = low_frequency_vectors @ low_frequency_vectors.T
    return candidate_idx, smoother, confidence


def _leave_one_out_sector_misfit(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
    graph_window: int = 60,
    refresh_interval: int = 5,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Causally compute five-bar graph leave-one-out residuals and confidence."""
    safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
    daily_return = safe_close.pct_change(fill_method=None).replace(
        [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
    )
    five_bar_return = safe_close.pct_change(5, fill_method=None).replace(
        [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
    )

    returns_array = daily_return.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    target_array = five_bar_return.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    sector_array = sector.to_numpy(dtype=object)

    n_rows, n_cols = returns_array.shape
    gap_array = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    confidence_array = np.zeros((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=float)
    models: dict[str, tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, float]] = {}

    first_ready = graph_window + 5
    for t in range(first_ready, n_rows):
        # End the graph sample five bars before the target period, preventing
        # the return being reconstructed from entering its own graph estimate.
        if (t - first_ready) % refresh_interval == 0:
            models = {}
            labels = sector_array[t]
            valid_labels = labels[~pd.isna(labels)]

            for label in pd.unique(valid_labels):
                sector_idx = np.flatnonzero(labels == label)
                if sector_idx.size < 5:
                    continue

                history = returns_array[t - 5 - graph_window : t - 5]
                model = _build_sector_spectral_model(history, sector_idx)
                if model is not None:
                    models[str(label)] = model

        if not models:
            continue

        current_target = target_array[t]
        for candidate_idx, smoother, confidence in models.values():
            y = current_target[candidate_idx]

            # The LOO projection is obtained from y = H y: remove the own-node
            # H_ii contribution before reconstructing each node from neighbors.
            if not np.all(np.isfinite(y)):
                continue

            diagonal = np.diag(smoother)
            denominator = 1.0 - diagonal
            if np.any(np.abs(denominator) < 0.05):
                continue

            projected = smoother @ y
            loo_prediction = (projected - diagonal * y) / denominator
            gap_array[t, candidate_idx] = y - loo_prediction
            confidence_array[t, candidate_idx] = confidence

    gap = pd.DataFrame(gap_array, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    confidence = pd.DataFrame(
        confidence_array, index=close.index, columns=close.columns
    )
    return gap, confidence


@register_factor
class LeaveOneOutSectorSpectralMisfit(BaseFactor):
    """Mean-reversion signal from stable sector spectral leave-one-out residuals."""

    factor_id = "leaveoneout_sector_spectral_misfit"
    name = "Leave-One-Out Sector Spectral Misfit"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Within each sector, estimates a trailing residual-correlation graph and "
        "uses its stable low-frequency normalized-Laplacian modes to produce a "
        "leave-one-out five-bar return reconstruction. Long lower graph-implied "
        "return gaps and short higher gaps, suppressing weak-eigengap graphs."
    )
    window_length = 70
    inputs = ["close", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        sector = data["sector"]
        gap, confidence = _leave_one_out_sector_misfit(close, sector)

        # Negative rank implements the intended convergence trade: names below
        # their graph-implied return receive the relatively larger long score.
        signal = -rank(gap)
        return signal.where(confidence > 0.0, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
